name: Thangamayil Jewellery Ltd
tagline: Madurai-anchored Tamil Nadu gold-jewellery retailer with a candid family management and a strong FY25-26 (revenue +28-45%, swung back to profit) - but ~6% EBITDA margins, gold-price-flattered topline and intensifying Kalyan/Titan competition in its home state cap the upside
business_overview: Thangamayil Jewellery is an organised jewellery chain with ~66 outlets (jewellery + silver) concentrated in southern and western Tamil Nadu, dominant in Madurai (~15% city share) and tier-2/3/rural towns. It is a largely plain-gold jeweller with a growing (~10% of revenue) non-gold/studded mix, run by three brothers (second/third generation now involved) with a track record of cutting their own pay and pausing expansion during past down-cycles.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 16,910 Cr (per screener; appears rich vs ~Rs 145 Cr EBITDA - treat with caution)
~Rs 4,911 Cr, +28% YoY; Q2 FY26 revenue +45% YoY to ~Rs 1,711 Cr; record Oct-2025 sales ~Rs 1,032 Cr
Q2 FY26 PAT ~Rs 58.5 Cr vs a ~Rs 17.4 Cr loss YoY; EBITDA margin ~6% (ex-customs duty ~6.1%)
Rs 510 Cr rights issue improved gearing to ~0.7x; working-capital borrowings up with gold inventory
fundamentals_narrative: FY25-26 has been strong: FY25 operating income +28% to ~Rs 4,911 Cr, Q2 FY26 revenue +45% and a swing from a YoY loss to a ~Rs 58.5 Cr profit on festive/record October sales, helped by a Rs 510 Cr rights issue that improved the capital structure (gearing ~0.7x). Management is unusually candid and has navigated past regulatory shocks (gold-import bans, 80:20 rule) by rationalising inventory and hedging ~60% of gold. But the model has hard limits: EBITDA margin is only ~6% (typical for gold retail), a large part of revenue 'growth' is simply the rising gold price rather than volume, the sector is fiercely competitive with Kalyan, Titan/Tanishq and Joyalukkas all expanding aggressively into Tamil Nadu, and Q1 FY26 margins were already down. The screener market cap (~Rs 16,910 Cr) looks inconsistent with ~Rs 145 Cr EBITDA and should be verified.
technical_read: Not independently pulled; the stock has hit multiple 20% upper circuits on record-sales prints and trades in a very wide 52-week band (~Rs 1,935-7,429).
sentiment_summary: Long-running 111-post thread (since 2011). The historical consensus (sagararya, Rohit_Kadam, ankitgupta, arcticglaze) is admiration for a candid, execution-focused family that came out of the 2013-14 gold-regulation crisis stronger with better inventory turns and lower debt. Recent posts (Arka, axsubram, Jitendrapd94) track the FY25-26 revenue acceleration, the swing back to profit, record October sales and new store adds; Niravkumar_Malani explains how high gold prices shift the mix toward studded jewellery. The only recent question (Aswin_MM, Aug 2026) is why Q1 FY26 margins slipped. No trusted-user participation.
community_signal: None from trusted users. The community read is a well-run regional jeweller executing well in a strong gold cycle, with no governance concerns but no unusual conviction.
bse_notes: No SEBI or fraud action found. Rs 510 Cr rights issue completed (improved gearing to ~0.7x). Promoters ~61.6%, 0% pledged. Management historically cut director salaries and paused expansion during loss-making periods; hedges ~60% of gold inventory. June-2025 ICRA rationale: 28% FY25 revenue growth, comfortable debt coverage.
bull_case: Strong FY25-26 execution: revenue +28-45% YoY, swing back to profit, record October-2025 sales (~Rs 1,032 Cr), new store additions
Candid, capital-disciplined family management with a proven ability to navigate gold-regulation shocks (2013-14) and a hedged inventory book
Dominant local brand in Madurai / southern TN (tier-2/3/rural), a large under-penetrated organised-jewellery opportunity
Rights issue has improved the balance sheet; growing non-gold/studded mix (~10%) is margin-accretive
bear_case: ~6% EBITDA margin is structural for gold retail - operating leverage is limited and pricing power is low
A large share of revenue 'growth' is the rising gold price, not volume - topline optics flatter the underlying business
Intensifying competition from Kalyan, Titan/Tanishq and Joyalukkas expanding into Tamil Nadu; Q1 FY26 margins already slipped
Reported market cap looks rich versus EBITDA - valuation may already price in the good cycle
thesis_fit: neither - a well-run but thin-margin regional gold retailer whose growth is partly gold-price-driven and whose end-market is getting more competitive; no credible path to a 10x in 2-3 years
verdict_headline: Candid management executing well through a strong gold cycle - but 6% margins, price-flattered growth and Kalyan/Titan competition in its home state make it a quality regional retailer, not a multibagger. thesis_fit neither, conviction Low-Medium
verdict_reasoning: First-time coverage. The recent trend is strong (revenue +28-45%, swing back to profit, record October sales) and management quality is a genuine positive.

But 'neither' fits: ~6% EBITDA margins are structural, a large part of the topline growth is the gold price rather than volume, and Kalyan/Titan/Joyalukkas are all expanding into Tamil Nadu - the model does not support a 10x, and the reported valuation already looks full.
No trusted-user signal; no conviction floor.

No red-flag tier (clean governance, no pledge, no SEBI action). thesis_fit neither; conviction Low-Medium. Not flagged for 30-day revisit (thesis_fit neither); recheck if the studded-mix shift materially lifts blended margins.

four_box.note: Dominant regional brand in an under-penetrated Tamil Nadu organised-jewellery market is a real tailwind; intensifying competition from Kalyan/Titan-Tanishq/Joyalukkas expanding into TN plus gold-price-driven (not volume) topline growth — tam weak; candid, capital-disciplined management with a hedged inventory book (~60%) is a real edge, but ~6% EBITDA margin is structural for gold retail with limited pricing power — moat weak; reported market cap 'looks rich versus EBITDA' — valuation no.
